body: Not sure who to CC, perhaps @asoldano?
Yeah, something we need to fix.

May be a property like `disable-quarkus-mappers` ? Otherwise it can be tricky if not impossible, as both the quarkus and the custom user mapper are all the custom providers for RestEasy, both competing for the same exception type

The other option is to check in Quarkus, before registering its own mapper if something else is available, but then Quarkus would need some RestEasy logic to see if the user mapper is competing with the Quarkus one or not...May be just checking the type var would be enough

@sberyozkin I don't understand JAX-RS, but would it help if RESTEasy treated the Quarkus providers as "built-in"? That's what they are, from my perspective. (Not sure if that wouldn't break something else :grin:)
@Ladicek Hi, then RestEasy would need to decide what to do with its built-in mappers if any, though it might work nicely, indeed Alessio and other RestEasy gurus would know :-)

Actually, the spec doesn't talk about built-ins when it discusses `ExceptionMapper`, and the implementation seems to only favour non-built-ins when comparing exceptions by class.

So even if the priority would favour a user mapper for `NotFoundException` it would not favour one for `Exception` which is more generic.

Now, do note that the `NotFoundExceptionMapper` only applies to the DEV mode.

We could perhaps only register it if we didn't find any user mapper that is more generic, but that would mean that the DEV mode is less useful when it comes to 404 because user mappers are likely to be less user-friendly.
@ronsigal , do you have any thoughts here?

Hi @Ladicek,

I'm not following the premise here. You said you created "my own NotFoundExceptionMapper" but that it is an "implementation of ExceptionMapper<Exception>". So the JAX-RS spec says your ExceptionMapper would not got used:

```
When choosing an exception mapping provider to map an exception, an implementation MUST use the
provider whose generic type is the nearest superclass of the exception. If two or more exception providers
are applicable, the one with the highest priority MUST be chosen as described in Section 4.1.3.
```

Why not create an ExceptionMapper<NotFoundExceptionMapper> and annotate it with a @Priority higher than the one in Quarkus?

What am I missing?

-Ron

Quarkus has one for `NotFoundException` (low prio, but nearest superclass), the user has one for `Exception` (high prio, but furthest superclass).

I guess the user would like his mapper to override the Quarkus one.

@ronsigal What you're suggesting is the workaround I was able to identify and use. (Fortunately, the Quarkus built-in exception mappers are `@Priority(Priorities.USER + 1)`, so I don't have to add `@Priority` myself.)

What I'd like to happen is if I define my own exception mapper (for a more general class), the Quarkus built-in exception mappers are not used. What @FroMage says, basically :-)
